title: Does my tool serve the HTML?
text: Someone assumed their tool sends back the widget's HTML directly. It doesn't, a separate resource serves that. So, how do you make a resource serve the widget's HTML? The two-part registration

title: Tool returns data, resource serves HTML
text: Is the core pattern. Part one, the tool, it declares a UI resource via meta.ui.resourceuri and its handler returns plain data, not the HTML. Part two, the resource registered separately, it serves the widget's HTML with the exact mime type text/html;profile=mcapp. The host sees that resource URI, fetches the resource, and renders it in an iframe. Piping the tool's return value in through an on tool result event. Inside the iframe, an app class bridges the two sides. Methods like send message, update model context, call server tool, and open link set up before it connects. One more step is mandatory. The iframe's content security policy blocks CDN script fetches, so the widget script bundle has to be inlined directly into the HTML at startup. Before

title: Route first: elicitation, widget, or text
text: Building a widget, route correctly. Elicitation is spec native zero UI code works in any compliant host. Use it for yes/no confirmation, short and unpicks, and flat forms. Build a widget only when the need can't be met by elicitation. Large or searchable lists that need scrolling, visual previews before choosing, charts and maps, and live updating progress. If none of those apply, skip the widget entirely. Text is faster to build and faster for the user. Five design rules that save rewrites. One widget per tool. The tool's description must mention the widget since that's what makes Cloud Reach for it. Graceful degradation is automatic. Hosts that don't support the app surface just render the tool's text content. Don't block on widget results for display-only tools. Return a text summary alongside so Cloud can keep reasoning. And follow the host's theme once connected. Instead of hardcoding one. Two ways to end up with the exact

title: Two causes, one blank rectangle
text: Same blank rectangle and no error message. Serve the widget with the wrong mime type and the host silently refuses to render it. Or leave the X-Taps bundle un-inlined, the iframe's content security policy blocks the CDN fetch, and the widget stays blank there, too. Same failure, two different causes, and the browser console won't tell you which one it was. An MCP app is just a server

title: The carry-out
text: With an extra resource. The tool still returns data, and it's the resource that serves the widget's HTML. Get the type or the bundle wrong, and it fails blank, not loud. Your turn. Paste this into

title: Your turn
text: Claude. Build an MCP app with a file picker widget that lets someone choose a file from a list a directory scan tool returns. Then check four things. Does it use two-part registration, a tool with meta.ui.resourceUri plus a separate resource? Does the resource use the exact mime type constant, not a hand-typed string? Is the X-Tags bundle inlined at startup instead of pulled from a CDN? And does the tool still return real text content alongside the widget, so a host without the app's surface see something useful? Get the type or the bundle wrong, and the widget renders blank. Same failure, no error either way. Return data, serve HTML, lay 'em in for bear.
